name: DeviceMock
description: A drawn device frame (phone, tablet, laptop, desktop, watch or browser window) around your content, which becomes the screen. The frame is plain CSS decoration with neutral bezels; the screen is a real container, so everything inside keeps its own semantics and focus order.

children.description: The content shown on the screen.

orientation.description: Turns a phone or a tablet on its side. Other devices ignore it.

label.description: Accessible name of the group, for example Mobile preview. Without it the frame adds nothing to the accessibility tree.

keyboard: Tab: moves through the focusable content inside the screen as if the frame were not there
requirements: The frame, notch, camera dots, stand and browser toolbar are aria-hidden decoration
The screen is a real div holding the children, so headings, forms and links inside keep their semantics
With label the root is a group named by it; without it the root is a plain div
Static: nothing moves, so there is no still switch
The frame scales down with its parent (width 100 percent up to a maximum) and never causes horizontal scroll
Forced colors: bezels keep a visible system-color border
screenReader: Announced as a group with the label when given, then the screen content in order

use_when: Showing how a screen looks on a phone, tablet, laptop or in a browser window
avoid_when: The device shape carries meaning the user must act on
